problem:
Let $X$ be the number obtained by a spinner with six sections labeled $1,2,3,4,5,6.$ The probability mass function $f(x)$ of $X$ is shown in the table below. What is $\text{Var}[X]?$

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ | $6$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $\frac{3}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{16}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{16}$ |

feedback.problem:
Let $X$ be the outcome of rolling an unfair five-sided die that follows the probability mass function $f(x)$ shown in the table below. What is $\text{Var}[X]?$

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{256}{625}$ | $\frac{256}{625}$ | $\frac{96}{625}$ | $\frac{16}{625}$ | $\frac{1}{625}$ |
feedback.worked_solution:
We can compute the variance of a discrete random variable $X$ using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

First, we compute $\text{E}[X].$ Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =0\cdot f(0)+1\cdot f(1)+2\cdot f(2)+3\cdot f(3)+4\cdot f(4) \\  & =0(\frac{256}{625})+1(\frac{256}{625})+2(\frac{96}{625})+3(\frac{16}{625})+4(\frac{1}{625}) \\  & =\frac{4}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={0}^{2}\cdot f(1)+{1}^{2}\cdot f(2)+{2}^{2}\cdot f(3)+{3}^{2}\cdot f(4)+{4}^{2}\cdot f(5) \\  & =0(\frac{256}{625})+1(\frac{256}{625})+4(\frac{96}{625})+9(\frac{16}{625})+16(\frac{1}{625}) \\  & =\frac{32}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{32}{25}-{(\frac{4}{5})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{32}{25}-\frac{16}{25} \\  & =\frac{16}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$
